findings.text: the wait hold now runs ahead of the existing-run guard at :1645 and hold_request_for_upstream writes the phase unconditionally through runs._mutate_pointer, so a re-dispatch of a node whose section waits read unmet rewrites whatever pointer carries that node, including an in-flight one, to awaiting-upstream and takes a running run off its lane.

the two waiting phase names are added as string literals in a second vocabulary rather than taken from reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:53, against the plan's rule that every phase reader reads them from that vocabulary, so a rename in queue_admission silently stops the watch line drawing a held request and nothing fails.

the manifest names neg-wiring.log as this round's control, but that log's header reads revision 06c368dce and its mutation removes two hold_request_for_upstream calls, while the reviewed head holds through the single call at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1597, so the control does not exercise the wiring it is offered for.

the manifest asserts the 23 failures are pre-existing because the same ids fail at HEAD~1, but no log in the run directory records that run; the base arm delta-base.log exercises 14 ids, so 9 of the head's 23 failures are argued rather than measured.

assert reading["classification"] == phase compares the classifier's output against the phase the test itself wrote into the record at :510, against the assertions independence rule; the companion assertion at :520 on the remedy string is the independent half of that arm.
